summary: Tax Mileage feature (backend engine + Mileage tab + Home pillar) verified end-to-end. Backend: 27/27 pytest pass (20 existing + 7 new Tax Mileage tests + 9 sub-cases). All target scenarios validated: GET /api/tax-mileage returns today/financial_year/logbook/method_comparison(logbook vs cents_per_km with recommend/label/difference)/odometer/vehicle sections; mixed trip 50km@60%=30 business km in tax-mileage AND in /api/reports & /api/dashboard (regression); FY 2026-27 cpk rate=0.91 with 5000km cap → max $4550 verified with a 6000km trip; logbook.complete=true for 120-day span with continuous 12-week (84-day) window selected; logbook.complete=false with <12 weeks; odometer discrepancy warning fires when GPS 5000km vs odometer 10000km (50% off); GET /api/export-mileage returns 200 text/csv with 'Motor Vehicle Report' and 'Method comparison'; existing /api/reports, /api/dashboard, /api/performance still work with mixed-aware business km. Frontend (Expo web, viewport 390x844): Home shows home-mileage-pillar with 'TAX MILEAGE · FY 2026-27' + estimated deduction + recommend chip; tapping navigates to /trips (Mileage tab). Mileage hub renders TODAY (50 km / 30 km business), 'WHICH METHOD IS BETTER?' comparison card (Logbook $0.00 vs Cents/km $27.30 with trophy 'Cents per kilometre — Potentially higher by $27.30'), ATO Logbook row (mileage-open-logbook), Vehicle row (mileage-open-vehicle) with visible odometer discrepancy warning, and 'Add trip' + 'GPS shift' buttons. Vehicle screen (/vehicle): filling veh-rego/veh-model/veh-year/veh-open-odo/veh-close-odo and tapping veh-save persists to /api/profile (verified via GET). Logbook screen (/logbook) opens with logbook-back and lists the journey. Entry trip (/entry?type=trip): trip-type selector Business/Mixed/Private, choosing Mixed reveals entry-business-pct, purpose chips entry-purpose-collect/deliver visible, saving a 25km/40% mixed/collect trip persists via /api/trips (business_pct=40.0, purpose='collect'). No red-screen errors. Existing calendar/DateField feature not re-tested per request.

action_items: None required for Tax Mileage — feature is working across backend + UI + persistence as specified.

Optional: silence 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated' RN-web warning by migrating pointerEvents={...} to style.pointerEvents on any custom components (grep the codebase; likely inside src/ui.tsx or a Modal wrapper).

critical_code_review_comments: backend/tax.py::best_logbook_window is well-scoped: only considers windows fully covered by the data span (start + 84 days <= last), and falls back to the whole set for <12-week data as an in-progress window. Returns a stable, deterministic pick (highest business-pct with total_km tiebreak).

backend/tax.py::method_comparison correctly prefers the logbook business_pct (when available), falls back to derived (business_km/total_km), then to profile.business_use_fallback. cpk cap at 5000 km and rate lookup by fy_start_year are correctly implemented.
backend/server.py::tax_mileage endpoint composes all four sub-sections via taxlib.tax_mileage and honours ref_date; excludes MongoDB _id via clean() everywhere. Good.
backend/tax.py::odometer_check safely handles the 'no readings' state and returns a prompt; discrepancy_pct rounded to 1dp; warning message uses '{gps_km:,.0f}' / '{odo_km:,.0f}' formatting — clean.

frontend/app/(tabs)/trips.tsx correctly gates on tm/method_comparison, uses testIDs mileage-open-logbook, mileage-open-vehicle, mileage-export, trips-add, gps-start, gps-tag-business, gps-tag-personal — all consistent with review request.
frontend/app/vehicle.tsx: veh-save wired to updateProfile({vehicle}); numeric fields parsed with parseFloat/parseInt and null-fallback; odometer fields use decimal-pad keyboard — good UX.

frontend/app/entry.tsx: entry-triptype-* switches purpose default correctly when toggling to personal; entry-business-pct clamped to 0–100 in save(); parses businessPct with sane fallback of 50 for mixed.
frontend/app/(tabs)/home.tsx home-mileage-pillar routes to '/trips' (tab); shows recommended deduction and business_pct/business_km — correct.

Storage-shape observation (already latent, not introduced by this feature): the app's storage layer JSON.parses values in localStorage — testing agents must JSON.stringify strings when priming gigtax.profile_id. This is app-standard behaviour, not a bug.

To activate a specific profile in the web preview, set localStorage BEFORE reload: window.localStorage.setItem('gigtax.profile_id', JSON.stringify('<pid>')) — the app JSON.parses stored values, so unquoted strings will trigger a benign parse warning and fall back to fresh onboarding.
